cards.text: Jesus and His disciples come to a place called Gethsemane. He tells them, 'Sit here while I pray.' Friend, this one's heavy, so I'm gonna tell it slow.
He takes Peter, James and John with Him. And Jesus begins to be deeply troubled and distressed.

cards.question: Jesus tells Peter, James and John, 'My soul is consumed with sorrow to the point of death.' What does He ask the three of them to do?

answers.text: Go back and get the others
Head into the city for help

cards.text: He goes a little farther and falls to the ground. He prays that, if it were possible, the hour would pass from Him.

cards.question: Jesus begins His prayer, 'Abba, Father.' True or false: He says all things are possible for His Father.

cards.text: Then He asks His Father, 'Take this cup from Me.'

cards.question: Jesus asks the Father to take the cup from Him. What does Jesus say right after that?

answers.text: He wants the Father's will over His own
He will wait until morning for an answer
He will keep asking until it's taken away

cards.text: Then Jesus gets up and goes back to Peter, James and John.

cards.question: Jesus asked them to keep watch. When He comes back, He finds Peter, James and John ___.

cards.text: Jesus asks Peter, 'Simon, are you asleep?' and then, 'Were you not able to keep watch for one hour?'

cards.question: Jesus tells Peter, James and John to watch and pray. What for?

answers.text: So they won't enter into temptation
So they can warn the other disciples
So His own prayer is answered sooner

cards.question: Jesus tells them that the spirit is willing, but the body is weak.

cards.text: Again Jesus goes away and prays, saying the same thing. Then He comes back a second time.

cards.question: When Jesus comes back the second time, Peter, James and John are awake and keeping watch.

cards.text: Sleeping AGAIN, because their eyes were heavy. Friend, heavy eyes are UNDEFEATED. Ask anybody who ever hit the snooze button 'just once.'

cards.question: Jesus finds Peter, James and John asleep a second time. How do they answer Him?

answers.text: They don't know what to answer

cards.text: When Jesus returns the third time, He says, 'Are you still sleeping and resting? That is enough! The hour has come.'

cards.question: Jesus tells Peter, James and John the hour has come. What does He say is happening to the Son of Man?

answers.text: He is betrayed into the hands of sinners
He is welcomed into the city by crowds
He is called up to teach at the temple

cards.question: Jesus says, 'Rise, let us go.' Then He tells them who is approaching: His ___.

cards.text: While Jesus is still speaking, Judas arrives. Judas, one of the Twelve, and he's got a crowd with him.

cards.question: The crowd with Judas didn't come to chat. What are they armed with?

cards.text: The crowd was sent from the chief priests, scribes, and elders. And Judas, the betrayer, had arranged a signal with them.

cards.question: What is Judas's signal to show the crowd which One to arrest?

cards.text: Judas goes directly to Jesus, says, 'Rabbi!' and kisses Him. Then the men seize Jesus and arrest Him.
Then one of the bystanders draws his sword. Things just got LOUD in Gethsemane.

cards.question: The bystander swings his sword. Who does he strike?
The bystander's sword strikes the high priest's servant and cuts off his ___.

cards.text: Jesus turns to the crowd with a question about all those swords and clubs.

cards.question: Jesus asks the crowd if they've come with swords and clubs to arrest Him as they would an ___.
Jesus says He was with them every day, teaching in the temple courts, and they never arrested Him.
They never arrested Jesus in the temple courts. So why does He say this arrest has happened?

answers.text: So the Scriptures would be fulfilled
Because Judas had a change of heart
Because the crowd had grown afraid

cards.question: Once Jesus is arrested, His disciples stay right by His side.

cards.text: Everyone deserted Him and fled. Then one young man who had been following Jesus, wearing a linen cloth around his body, gets caught by the crowd.

cards.question: The crowd catches hold of the young man in the linen cloth. So what does he do? He ___.

cards.text: He pulls free of the linen cloth and runs away naked. Think about it, friend. The crowd grabbed a whole man and walked away holding... LAUNDRY.
We'll stop here for tonight, friend. Mark isn't close to finished with this one.

findings.problem: The question says Jesus tells Peter, James and John to watch and pray. In the BSB, Jesus addresses Simon by name in 14:37 and keeps speaking in 14:38 without saying who else He means. The card names all three as the people spoken to, which the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: 'Sleeping AGAIN, because their eyes were heavy.' 'Friend, heavy eyes are UNDEFEATED.' 'Ask anybody who ever hit the snooze button 'just once.''

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess Jesus' exact word, outlaw, against enemy and invader. All three fit the line, so the card tests wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning they can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: 'He pulls free of the linen cloth and runs away naked.' 'Think about it, friend.' 'The crowd grabbed a whole man and walked away holding... LAUNDRY.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The line 'We'll stop here for tonight, friend' assumes the baker's time of day. Papa Dorin isn't told that.

rule.text: What he doesn't know: anything about the individual baker that he hasn't been told, such as their streak, their mood, the time of day or how they've done before.

findings.problem: This last story card is only the story-isn't-over line, which the rules allow. It tells no verse, but it cites Mark 14:52, and card 16 already tells that verse. The citation rule says a story card cites the verses it tells, no wider and no narrower. The JSON format needs a verses value on every card.
findings.question: What should a story card cite when it holds only the story-isn't-over line and tells no verse: the passage's last verse, no reference, or something else?
